notes: TL;DR: Infra-heavy code-search shop. Very sensitive to p95 latency and cost per query. Wants private VPC with local GPUs for re-ranking stage.
Company background: enterprise dev tools vendor, 400 engineers, monorepo-heavy (several ~1TB repos). Primary product: developer search + assistant for internal dev teams.
Embeddings footprint: currently ~45M vectors (function-level granularity), expected growth to 120M in 6-9 months. Re-index cadence: nightly full pass + continuous deltas (~10k updates/day).
Latency targets: p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 200ms end-to-end for code search queries (ANN lookup + re-ranker). Reranker model budgeted for <= 150ms on CPU/GPU hybrid paths.
Cost sensitivity: target cost per query <= $0.01 (avg) when amortized across bulk usage; willing to trade batch latency for cost in background jobs but interactive search must be fast.

Preferred architecture: vector store for ANN (sharded by repo/team) + lightweight FAISS/PQ quantization for footprint; re-ranking as a second-stage small LLM (quantized) run on dedicated GPU pool; prefix caching for hot queries.

Integrations: Kafka for ingestion (they want Redwood to accept delta stream and provide idempotent upserts), SCIM for user sync, SAML SSO (Okta), retention policies per region (EU data must remain in eu-1).
Security ask: SOC2 report required, KMS integration for keys, detailed audit logs for every inference call, support for retention & deletion requests within 30 days.
Quote: Tech lead (Ravi Patel) — 'If p95 climbs above ~200ms devs start ignoring search. We need predictable tail latency, not average miracles.'

Current stack: PoC with Pinecone for ANN, Redis for cache, in-house re-ranker (DistilBERT) on EC2, CI pipeline for nightly index builds. Considering Redwood to remove operational overhead and add re-ranking on GPU + unified rollout controls.
Competitive pressure: evaluating Redwood vs managed vector DB + custom re-ranker; key differentiator is Redwood's private deployment + rollback/traceability for model rollouts.

POC success criteria (agreed): ingest 20M vectors in under 6 hours, p95 end-to-end <= 200ms on 95th percentile of a 1k qps synthetic trace, cost per query estimate validated in billing model, SSO and audit log ingestion validated.

Notes from 2026-03-05 call: AE demo went well; security asked for SOC2 AICPA docs and KMS diagram. SE asked for sample reindex-runbook and expected storage footprint numbers. Asked for estimated time to restore partial index from snapshot (<= 30m target).
Follow-ups: share reindex runbook + sample Kafka connector (by 2026-03-09), send SOC2 packet and HSM/KMS integration docs (done 2026-03-06), schedule infosec review 2026-03-12.
Short-term decisions pending: exact model for reranker (customer prefers 3B quantized variant or smaller distilled model), whether to use Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/caching in POC.

POC constraints: cannot access raw source code outside VPC; embeddings must be computed inside customer network or via bring-your-own-embedder flow. Customer will run an embedder job in their infra and push vectors to Redwood private cluster.
Possible risks flagged: frequent reindexing may blow token quotas if Redwood hosted embedder used; must validate BYO-embed path and safe dedupe/merge semantics for vectors.
